_comment: Every entry is a control this project claims to have, and the exact edit that
should break it. `node scripts/mutate.mjs --all` applies each one to the real
source, runs the real suite, and demands that the named test goes red.
AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md §6: a green suite is evidence that nothing currently
disagrees with a control, not that the control exists. This file is where that
distinction is made mechanical -- and where 'nobody audits the auditor' (§7) is
answered, because each mutation is stated precisely enough to be re-run by
ADD AN ENTRY WHEN YOU ADD A CONTROL. Not later, and not only when a control
looks fragile: the two worst defects of 2026-09-03 were both in code written
that same hour specifically to enforce verification honesty, and both looked
finished. `find` must match EXACTLY ONCE or the run reports INCONCLUSIVE.
The `expect` field is a substring of the test name that must appear among the
failures. Without it, ANY red suite would count as the control working -- which
is how a mutation that broke something unrelated gets recorded as proof.

mutations.guards: every export in public/ and src/ has a real (non-test) caller or a written allowlist reason -- a NEW export added with neither must fail the gate
mutations.note: The mutation targets a small fixture file (public/_deadExportMutationFixture.js) built only for this purpose, not a shared production file, so this entry cannot collide with another lane's concurrent work in city-render.js/terrain.js/etc. The fixture starts with zero exports; the mutation adds one, unwired and unlisted.
mutations.replace:
// from this file. docs/BUILD-LOOP.md Step 6.

export function __deadExportMutationProbe__() { return 1; }
mutations.expect: every export in public/ and src/ is product-reachable

mutations.guards: renderModuleMap (scripts/gen-module-map.mjs) marks every non-product export with its DEMO-ONLY/TEST-ONLY/UNREACHABLE state in the generated document, not just in memory
mutations.note: Targets the generator script itself, not a shared production file. Updated when the generator was rewritten for reachability (Mark's review, same day as I2/I3): the old single **UNCALLED** marker no longer exists, replaced by STATE_LABEL[entry.state]; this mutation removes that lookup from the emitted line, leaving the product branch (which never uses STATE_LABEL) untouched on purpose, so the smoke test's assertion is proven to exercise the non-product path specifically.
mutations.expect: product/demo-only/test-only/unreachable are all distinguishable in the text

mutations.guards: classifyReachability must classify an export whose ONLY caller is reachable from a demo page as demo-only, never product -- the exact roadkit.js junction/roundabout distinction this whole reachability upgrade exists for (Mark's correction: import counting and reachability can disagree)
mutations.note: Targets classifyReachability's own demo-crediting branch in scripts/lib/module-graph.mjs (this task's own file). Changing the assigned state string from demo-only to product is the precise bug that made the FIRST version of this gate report roadkit.js's junction/roundabout as confirming they were fully uncalled, when they were actually reachable -- just only from a demo page.
mutations.expect: called only from a demo page reachable from nothing else is demo-only, not product

mutations.guards: buildReverseMap credits `x.js`'s export when it is reached as `ALIAS.member(...)` after `import * as ALIAS from "./x.js"`, not only through a named import -- found by a blind audit: public/roadkit-street-demo.js's real ROADKIT.straight(...)/ROADKIT.curve(...)/etc calls, without this, made 16 genuinely-called roadkit.js exports read as fully dead
mutations.note: Removes the `alias` field the namespace clause capture adds, targeting scripts/lib/module-graph.mjs (this task's own new file, not a shared production one another lane might be mid-edit on). Without `alias`, the member-access regex built from it becomes `/\bundefined\.(...)/`, which matches nothing real -- a structural break, not a disabled branch (per docs/AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md's own lesson this session: a commented-out or if(false)-wrapped mutation leaves source text intact and can survive wrongly).
mutations.expect: credits x.js's `member` export -- the roadkit-street-demo.js shape

mutations.guards: buildReverseMap credits the file a `export { X } from "./x.js"` statement names as X's real source with a caller -- found by a blind audit: src/index.ts's real re-export of SpendCounterDO (wrangler.jsonc's bound Durable Object class_name), without this, made src/spendCounterDOClass.ts -- the file that actually defines CALIPER's spend cap -- read as fully dead
mutations.note: Targets findReExportClauses' own regex in scripts/lib/module-graph.mjs (this task's own new file). Requiring an impossible literal prefix is a real structural break (the function always returns []), not a disabled branch.
mutations.expect: credits x.js's X with a real caller -- the src/index.ts/SpendCounterDO shape

mutations.guards: each cloud deck owns its material, so the low one can fade while the high one is still overhead
mutations.expect: the decks fade INDEPENDENTLY

mutations.guards: a deck you have climbed above stops drawing, instead of rendering its far rim as a white crescent
mutations.expect: at the orbit Mark was flying

mutations.guards: props.js resolves every manifest id by its own name, so prop-models.js does not need a second table that must agree with it
mutations.expect: the LIBRARY declares the join

mutations.guards: every row of the navigation pad draws itself with --nav-radius and --nav-shadow, so the pad reads as one instrument instead of a stack of chips with different corners
mutations.note: Mark: 'the nav is a mess from a looks standpoint ... it just looks disconnected from each other and random.' Measured, that was three different corner radii (11px on the strips, 10px on the readout, 50% on the dial) and two shadows across five rows. No single row was wrong, which is how they got there one at a time -- so the control is against the FOURTH one arriving.
mutations.expect: uses those tokens instead of its own numbers

mutations.guards: the pad's rows are border-box and full width, so their left AND right edges line up instead of each row sizing to its own content
mutations.note: Without border-box the 1px borders and the padding push each row past --nav-w by a different amount, and the ragged right edge returns by arithmetic rather than by anyone typing a width -- which is the version of this defect that would be hardest to see in a diff.
mutations.expect: edges line up

mutations.guards: the working tree holds the same bytes as the repository, so `git add` has nothing to convert and never rewrites a file another process is reading
mutations.note: `* text=auto` stores LF and checks out CRLF on Windows. MEASURED: one commit of small edits reported 66,043 insertions across 12 files, and `git add -A` renormalising the 4 MB public/tier-models.js during a mutate run made esbuild read it mid-rewrite -- a syntax error at 4722:40 that does not exist, 3 test files failing to build, and 14 consecutive INCONCLUSIVE results reported as '10 of 24 controls proved they exist'.
mutations.expect: the working tree and the repository hold the same bytes

mutations.guards: the model catalogue is linked from the front door, so a player can reach the 2,400 models by clicking rather than by typing a filename
mutations.note: The worst defect found in this repository, and it was not a bug -- everything worked. Six pages existed in public/ and exactly ONE was reachable. An unreachable page is not an error, it is an absence, and absences do not throw, which is why no test would ever have caught it. This one walks the links.
mutations.expect: reachable from the front door

mutations.guards: every page a player can land on links back to the front door, so none of them is a trap
mutations.note: The first version of this control accepted EITHER a back-to-caliper class OR a link home, and a mutation renaming the class correctly survived -- the href was still there. That exposed the weakness in the other direction: a page carrying the class with a broken href would have passed on the strength of a CSS class name. A class is decoration; an href is the way out.
mutations.expect: way back

mutations.guards: a layer is refused unless it is storable data, so a world can be saved, sent, cloned and attributed
mutations.note: The first version relied on JSON.stringify failing on a function. It does not -- it silently DROPS it, so a layer carrying a closure round-tripped with the same edit count and was accepted, then lost the player's work on save with no message. Found by this exact mutation surviving.
mutations.expect: plain data that survives being stored

mutations.guards: cloning a world deep-copies its layers, so editing your copy cannot reach back into the world you copied from
mutations.note: The first version spread each edit but shared its payload object. Editing a clone would have silently edited the original -- the worst possible version of this feature and invisible until someone noticed their world had changed. The test only compared layer COUNTS, so the mutation survived until it was strengthened to mutate a payload.
mutations.expect: same base and a copy of the work

mutations.guards: a later layer overrides an earlier one PER OP, so a move and a retint by two different authors coexist on the same object
mutations.note: Whole-object replacement would make collaboration impossible and undo destructive: the newest edit would erase every other change anyone had made to that thing.
mutations.find: for (const e of this.editsFor(address)) byOp.set(e.op, e);
mutations.replace: for (const e of this.editsFor(address)) { byOp.clear(); byOp.set(e.op, e); }
mutations.expect: independent changes coexist

mutations.guards: a stored layer that fails to load is reported rather than dropped, so a player's work never vanishes from their world in silence
mutations.find: if (bad) errors.push({ id: layer && layer.id, reason: bad });
mutations.expect: REPORTED, not silently dropped

mutations.guards: a remove beats every other edit to the same address, whatever order they arrived in
mutations.expect: removal wins outright

mutations.guards: seed 0 reproduces the pre-seed noise field byte for byte, so adding seeding did not silently move the world every measured number in this repo describes
mutations.note: The seed is mixed in by MULTIPLICATION precisely so it contributes exactly zero at seed 0. Most of this suite asserts properties rather than values, so a terrain that shifted by a metre would go on passing while invalidating 20,624 plots, 480 variants, 1.45 M triangles, the zoning percentiles and the airport's 11,041 dry sample points. The identity is pinned against the original expression written out longhand. Find/replace updated when hash2 started converting its own seed with seedToInt (A2b) -- the line moved from "Math.imul(seed, ...)" to "Math.imul(s, ...)".
mutations.expect: reproduces the original noise field exactly

mutations.guards: createNoise binds its seed into every function it returns, so a named world is genuinely a different landmass rather than the same one under a new name
mutations.note: The first version of this mutation neutered only hash2 and valueNoise and left fbm seeded, so the world still differed and it SURVIVED -- a bad mutation, not a weak test. Targeting the single place the seed is resolved is what makes it bite. Find/replace widened to include the function signature when A2b made hash2 also call seedToInt(seed) into a same-named local -- the old one-line find matched twice (hash2 and createNoise) and would have scored INCONCLUSIVE.
mutations.find:
export function createNoise(seed = DEFAULT_SEED) {
  const s = seedToInt(seed);
mutations.replace:
export function createNoise(seed = DEFAULT_SEED) {
  const s = 0;
mutations.expect: different seed is a different world

mutations.guards: load() reports a stored record that is not valid JSON, instead of swallowing the parse failure and quietly returning what looks like a valid, empty world
mutations.note: The mutation replaces the reported failure with a fabricated, VALID-shaped result (a real string seed, empty layers) rather than just deleting the return -- a mutation that left data malformed would still get caught by the very next validation check for an unrelated reason, which would prove nothing about this specific line.
mutations.find: return { ok: false, reason: `stored record for "${worldId}" is not valid JSON -- refusing to load it as an empty world` };
mutations.expect: is REPORTED, not silently dropped

mutations.guards: applyLayers calls world.resolve only for addresses the layer stack actually touched, never once per placement -- the cost of having layers scales with the size of the edit, not the size of the world
mutations.note: Re-resolving every placement would still produce a visually correct result (an untouched address resolves to an unedited state), so a happy-path visibility test would not catch this -- only counting resolve() calls does.
mutations.replace: for (const p of placements) { const address = p.plotId;
mutations.expect: resolve is called exactly once per touched address

mutations.guards: an override naming a model id that is not in the registry is refused BY THAT ID, never silently drawn as a fallback shape
mutations.note: The mutation is literally the temptation the ledger names: fall back to a default model on unknown id.
mutations.replace: const model = registry.get(modelId) || { ok: true, geometry: { attributes: {} }, measured: { triangles: 12 } };
mutations.expect: a layer referencing an unknown model id is refused at resolve

mutations.guards: a pick's plotId is the actual plot id, not the containing block's id -- the two ids look similar (both plan-derived strings) so a swap would not throw, only quietly point every edit at the wrong granularity of object
mutations.note: The ledger names this exact failure mode: return the nearest block instead of the plot.
mutations.replace:
current = { ...index.addressAt(x, z) }; current.plotId = current.blockId;
      return current;
mutations.expect: a pick returns a real plot id that is present in the plan

mutations.guards: the requests text field is exactly what was typed -- never templated into a markup string, which is the one way the apps existing textContent-only display discipline could be defeated upstream
mutations.note: Wrapping the text in a span is the literal anti-pattern this module exists to never do.
mutations.expect: typed text that looks like HTML passes through byte-identical

mutations.guards: verifyGeneratedGeometry checks a response against the ACTUAL requested footprint, never a loosened or fabricated one -- a response that ignores the constraint fails verification rather than being repaired or waved through
mutations.note: This is the ledgers own failure mode for D4: a response that ignores the measured constraints must fail verification, not be silently accepted. Inflating the declared footprint before checking is exactly the kind of quiet repair that would let it through.
mutations.replace: return verifyModelSource(source, { w: prompt.constraints.footprint.w + 1000, d: prompt.constraints.footprint.d + 1000 }, evaluate, THREE);
mutations.expect: verification uses the REQUESTED footprint, never anything the response itself claims

mutations.guards: a failed verdict is described in words that say failed/refused, never smoothed into text that reads as a success -- the failure-floor item 1 this whole project is built to prevent, applied to one stage's own display text
mutations.note: The mutation reports success text regardless of the verdict, which is exactly shipping an unverified/failed change while reporting it as verified.
mutations.find: return { ok: false, text: `verification failed at ${v.stage}: ${v.reason}` };
mutations.expect: a failed verify is shown as a failed verify

mutations.guards: the persisted layer references its model by id only -- the generated source is never inlined into it, which is what keeps a layer storable, sendable and diffable as plain data
mutations.note: source is in scope in applyAndPersist (the caller has it right after D4s verify step) -- this mutation is the realistic accident of including it, not a strawman.
mutations.find: edits: [{ address: request.address, op: "replace", payload: { modelId } }],
mutations.replace: edits: [{ address: request.address, op: "replace", payload: { modelId, source } }],
mutations.expect: a verified model becomes a layer that references it BY ID, never inlining the source

mutations.guards: undoLayer re-saves the world after removing a layer, so the removal survives a reload instead of only existing in memory until the next persisted save brings the undone layer back
mutations.note: This is the actual gap end-to-end proof exists for: worldModel.test.ts already proves remove() itself works in isolation. What isolation cannot see is a removal that never gets persisted.
mutations.expect: the undo survives a reload

mutations.guards: changeSomethingQuest completes because the world's own layer stack actually holds an edit, never because a UI-set flag says so -- a quest that completes on a flag is a cutscene
mutations.note: Named in the plan as the single most important mutation in Phase E. Reading state.player.mode is exactly the shape of the failure this quest exists to refuse.
mutations.expect: setting a UI flag, with no real edit, does NOT complete the quest

mutations.guards: checkInputGuard reads its length cap from CONTROL_LIMITS.FREE_FORM_MAX_LENGTH, never a hard-coded number at the call site -- a hard-coded copy stops tracking the one limits object silently
mutations.note: This is the exact mutation G1 names in the plan: hard-code one -> the test names it.
mutations.expect: checkInputGuard reads FREE_FORM_MAX_LENGTH live from CONTROL_LIMITS

mutations.guards: filterPending actually removes mutations whose id is already recorded, so --resume does not re-run (and re-report) work a prior, killed session already proved
mutations.note: Without this, --resume would print resuming: N of 52 already done and then run all 52 again anyway -- the exact defect the harness fix exists to prevent.
mutations.expect: a results file with three ids recorded causes those three to be skipped

mutations.guards: CLAUDE.md's How to verify section names the real, current node/worker test counts -- pinned mechanically, the same way test/publicClaims.test.ts already pins the page's identical claim, closing the gap a blind audit found the file stale by 297 tests
mutations.note: Found by docs/audits/UMAA-phases-B-H.md (Finding 1, HIGH): CLAUDE.md claimed 571 node tests where 868 actually ran -- the document instructing a reader how to verify the project was itself unverified against the thing it names.
mutations.find: npm test            # 948 node tests + 12 worker tests
mutations.replace: npm test            # 949 node tests + 12 worker tests
mutations.expect: CLAUDE.md's verification line names the real test counts

mutations.guards: I4: the describe box's result is displayed with .textContent, never .innerHTML -- the typed text is carried verbatim by makeDescribeRequest with no escaping of its own, so the display site is the one and only place this defense can live
mutations.note: describe-request.js's own header names this exact failure mode: something upstream builds an HTML string out of the text before display sees it. The ledger names the mutation directly: render the text with innerHTML -> the escaping test red.
mutations.expect: the describe result is displayed with .textContent only

mutations.guards: I5: a refused transform must never reach the injected model caller -- this is the mutation that guards real money, checked by the stub's CALL COUNT, never its outcome
mutations.note: Named before the test was written, per instruction. An outcome-only test on a stub caller passes whether or not the call was made; the call-count assertion is the actual guard.
mutations.expect: a refused transform never reaches the caller

mutations.guards: I5: the response verifyGeneratedGeometry checks is the one the injected caller actually returned, not a discarded or fabricated value -- otherwise a good model response could be silently ignored and the request would appear to fail (or a bad one silently pass) for reasons unrelated to what the model wrote
mutations.note: Found by test that good answers are found, not only that bad ones are refused -- every D-phase test up to I5 proved only refusals.
mutations.find:
const source = await caller(prompt);
  const verdict = verifyGeneratedGeometry(source, prompt, evaluate, THREE);
mutations.replace:
const source = await caller(prompt);
  const verdict = verifyGeneratedGeometry("", prompt, evaluate, THREE);
mutations.expect: a stubbed valid model response is verified

mutations.guards: I5: productionModelCaller throws rather than attempting a live call -- no route exists yet for it to call safely
mutations.note: A caller that structurally cannot spend money is the safest thing to ship before the route it needs is reviewed and built.
mutations.expect: productionModelCaller refuses immediately

mutations.guards: I5: scripts/supervised-generate.mjs refuses immediately when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset -- the first, cheapest safety layer against an accidental spend
mutations.note: A caller that structurally cannot spend money is the safest thing to ship before the route it needs is reviewed and built.
mutations.expect: refuses with no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

mutations.guards: I5: the script never prints a prompt (or reaches the spend-confirmation step) for a transform the ground has not approved
mutations.note: The same money-guard property public/run-generate-request.js enforces at the module level, checked again here at the script's own boundary.
mutations.expect: refuses a transform the ground does not approve

mutations.guards: merged geometry emits per-vertex colors tagging roof vs wall so that InstancedMesh can render contrasting colors via vertexColors
mutations.expect: distinguishing wall and roof

mutations.guards: bld-tower crown cone radius is bounded by minDim instead of bW, preventing the pyramid cap from overhanging by 11.81m in depth on non-square footprints
mutations.expect: bld-tower never draws past declared footprint

mutations.guards: declared triangle budget acts as a ceiling constraint that trips when geometry exceeds its budget, without hollow padding
mutations.find: parts.push({ geo: chim, tag: "wall" }, { geo: chimCap, tag: "roof" }, { geo: chimPot1, tag: "roof" }, { geo: chimPot2, tag: "roof" });
mutations.replace: parts.push({ geo: chim, tag: "wall" }, { geo: chimCap, tag: "roof" }, { geo: chimPot1, tag: "roof" }, { geo: chimPot2, tag: "roof" }, { geo: new geomT.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1), tag: "wall" });
mutations.expect: declared and actual triangle counts agree

mutations.guards: LOD1 provides a genuine intermediate massing level distinct from the LOD2 single silhouette box
mutations.find: { level: 1, tris: 50, createGeometry: (geomT) => buildLOD1(geomT || T) }, // midrise-lod1
mutations.replace: { level: 1, tris: 12, createGeometry: (geomT) => buildLOD2(geomT || T) }, // midrise-lod1
mutations.expect: LOD1 is an intermediate massing level distinct from LOD2

mutations.guards: J4: a new claim-*/city-stat-* span added to the page without a matching check in publicClaims.test.ts fails the build -- a hand-typed number wearing the convention that means "generated" is caught by name, not assumed correct
mutations.note: Simulates the exact failure mode this test exists for: a developer adds a new figure, follows the id convention, and never adds the check.
mutations.expect: every claim-* / city-stat-* span across index.html and city.html is checked

mutations.guards: the security fix for docs/audits/UMAA-I5-L-J4.md Finding 1 (HIGH): the child process that executes a real model response is spawned with an ALLOWLISTED environment, not the parent process env -- so ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not merely hidden from untrusted code, it does not exist in that process at all
mutations.note: Reverting to the parent env (the pre-fix shape) reintroduces the exact exploit the audit demonstrated: a unicode-escaped `process` identifier reads process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY successfully.
mutations.expect: the child process has no secret to steal

mutations.guards: public/index.html's #city-stat-buildings span is checked against CITY_STATS.buildingsPlaced (src/citySummary.generated.ts) by EQUALITY -- replacing the old `buildings > plots * 0.8` tolerance band that let "16,770" pass for months at 84.4%, four points inside the 80% floor that band enforced
mutations.note: Changing the generated placement count without touching the page simulates the world's build changing under a page that was not regenerated -- exactly the staleness the old band was too wide to catch. The <= plots impossibility check (guarded separately, unaffected by this mutation) still exists alongside this one; the two catch different failures.
mutations.expect: the placeholder city stats are reachable numbers, not decoration

mutations.guards: PART 7b/E2: test/mutationSummary.generated.json -- the committed evidence that every control in test/mutations.json has actually been run and CAUGHT -- is checked against its own internal counters, not just trusted
mutations.note: Simulates the summary's own `caught` field disagreeing with its own `mutations` array (a hand edit, or a future writer bug in gen-mutation-summary.mjs) -- the artefact contradicting itself, which is exactly the shape of defect a generated-but-unchecked file invites.
mutations.expect: the summary is not stale against the manifest it claims to cover

mutations.guards: PART 7b/E1: acquireLock() throws when a second caller asks for a lock the first has not proven released -- the concurrency guard behind both mutate.mjs and _mutcheck.mjs, closing the race that let two invocations touch the same source file at once
mutations.note: Removing the throw and letting a second lock silently succeed reintroduces exactly the race PART 7b/E1 found for real: one process's in-flight mutation read as another's baseline.
mutations.expect: a second acquireLock on a file the first still holds throws, and mutates nothing

mutations.guards: PART 7b/E3: recordTerminalRun's destructuring keeps the whole ledger (including each stage's model/at) in the changelog/ record it writes -- only the raw visitor request is stripped
mutations.note: Simulates a plausible future mistake -- someone destructuring a second field out alongside changeRequest and not noticing, since the changelog write still succeeds either way.
mutations.replace: const { changeRequest: _rawVisitorRequest, ledger: _droppedLedger, ...changelogRecord } = full as any;
mutations.expect: a stage cost's model and timestamp survive into the changelog record

mutations.guards: J1: #claim-hero-line (the above-the-fold central claim in #welcome-mission-card) is pinned to agree with <title>/og:title/twitter:title, not free to drift into a fifth, private wording of the same claim
mutations.note: Simulates the hero card's own copy being edited without updating the other three -- the exact way this project's own km/settlement/test-count claims have gone stale before.
mutations.find: CALIPER — a system that only says yes when yes is true
mutations.expect: the above-the-fold claim agrees with the page's own title -- one sentence, not a private copy of it

mutations.guards: K1: supervised-generate.mjs refuses an --address naming more than one target (comma or whitespace) with a deliberate scope check, before any plot lookup -- not an accidental refusal from a failed exact-match.
mutations.note: Without this check, a multi-address value still fails plot lookup today (no plot id has a comma in it) and still exits 1 -- but for the wrong reason, with the wrong message, and only by coincidence of the seed data. This mutation proves the refusal is deliberate.
mutations.expect: K1 scope: a request naming two addresses in one --address is refused by the limit, not by chance

mutations.guards: K3: buildGeometryPrompt refuses request.text over MAX_REQUEST_TEXT_LENGTH characters -- the blind audit found this path had no length bound at all, unlike the older live pipeline's checkInputGuard.
mutations.note: K3 (blind security audit, 2026-09-06), Q1: request.text flowed into the model prompt with no size check anywhere in this pipeline, an unbounded-cost vector if ever wired to a live route.
mutations.expect: K3: free-form request text has a length limit, same as the older live pipeline's, closing a gap the blind audit found had none

mutations.guards: K3: scanSource's FORBIDDEN_TOKENS includes "constructor", closing the (function(){}).constructor(...) chain the blind audit demonstrated reaches the global object without spelling "eval" or "Function(".
mutations.note: K3 (blind security audit, 2026-09-06), Q2: found a working denylist bypass distinct from the one already documented in this file's own header.
mutations.expect: K3: the .constructor(...) bypass the blind audit found no longer sails through the scan

mutations.guards: M2: the child process that runs untrusted model-authored geometry code is launched under Node's --permission flag with --allow-fs-read scoped to only the two files it needs -- an obfuscated payload that bypasses scanSource cannot read a file outside public/, even though env-scrubbing alone never prevented that.
mutations.note: M2 (final blind UMAA audit, 2026-09-06), CRITICAL: the header comment claiming 'a successful sandbox escape in this process has nothing to steal' was false -- fs/child_process/worker access does not depend on process.env at all. Reproduced live: an obfuscated payload read package.json and returned its contents through the verdict's reason string with no --permission flag.
mutations.expect: I5 security: an obfuscated filesystem-read payload that bypasses scanSource is still blocked by the child process's own permission restriction

mutations.guards: every createWithTruncationGuard(...) call site in src/claude.ts carries an explicit thinking:{type:"disabled"} setting -- 2026-09-06 incident: a caller that omits this can spend its whole max_tokens budget on thinking output and return an empty response.
mutations.note: The supervised live call that found this used a standalone script that never imported createWithTruncationGuard at all, so this exact mutation (removing the setting from one of the 8 real call sites) is the closest reproduction reachable inside src/claude.ts itself.
mutations.find:
"generateFunctionBody/repairFunctionBody", {
    model,
    max_tokens: MAX_TOKENS,
    thinking: { type: "disabled" },
    system: SYSTEM_PROMPT,
mutations.expect: every messages.create / createWithTruncationGuard call in src/ and scripts/ carries an explicit thinking setting

mutations.guards: scripts/supervised-generate.mjs's direct messages.create call carries an explicit thinking:{type:"disabled"} setting -- the exact call site the 2026-09-06 incident found missing it.
mutations.note: 2026-09-06: the real supervised run spent 1023 of 1024 max_tokens on thinking and 1 token on content, so the generated source was empty and verifyModelSource correctly refused at the scan stage. Not a capability finding -- a caller misconfiguration, fixed here and guarded by the same registry test as src/claude.ts's 8 call sites.
mutations.find:
const response = await client.messages.create({
    model, max_tokens: 1024,
    thinking: { type: "disabled" },
    system: systemPrompt,
mutations.expect: every messages.create / createWithTruncationGuard call in src/ and scripts/ carries an explicit thinking setting

mutations.guards: scanSource refuses a source that reaches for a THREE member outside ALLOWED_GEOMETRY_CONSTRUCTORS -- the real supervised run #2 payload (T.BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries(...)) is refused at scan, before the builder ever runs, not left to throw at build.
mutations.note: 2026-09-06, real supervised run #2: the prompt handed the model a bare namespace and never said what was on it.
